headline: More than two dozen US lawmakers have asked the aviation regulator to pause a new AI tool that helps manage air traffic around Washington, citing safety concerns.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a named AI tool in live air-traffic use and a formal congressional request, though officials say it only advises controllers.
importance_line: Passengers and controllers around Washington are the first affected, and the FAA plans to widen the tool to other regions under an $875 million, 12-year contract awarded in June to Air Space Intelligence, but officials say it only advises controllers and the lawmakers' complaint that no safety reports have been shown has not yet been answered.
summary: Reuters reports that more than two dozen lawmakers, including Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Don Beyer and Senator Chris Van Hollen, asked the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in a letter to pause the use of an AI tool that uses predictive analytics to help manage flights in the Washington area, saying they have seen no safety evaluation or testing reports and no plan to train safety staff, and want an answer by 19 Oct 2026. Sean Duffy, the US transportation secretary, called the tool essentially "dumb AI" and said controllers stay in charge, and the Department of Transportation says it makes scheduling recommendations but does not actively manage planes.
